notes: Credits use the catalog’s stated semester hours. Bundle credits belong to requirement nodes; individual amounts are supplied only when independently stated by a course catalog. Unverified alternative-course amounts and variable-credit scalar amounts remain unknown.
Course categories are editorial taxonomy. Outcomes summarize explicit program-overview statements; they are not measured graduate outcomes.
All major-page tables and policy references are represented. Partial status does not imply that the universitywide degree curriculum is complete.

Universitywide and NUpath criteria are now represented through verified shared policy bindings. The major-page reference notes describe what that page incorporates; linked policy rules appear separately in the resolved graph.

Open subject/level ranges, explicit grade/overlap limits and advisor-approved substitutions are represented criteria, not missing invented finite course lists. Individual approvals and registration eligibility remain governed by those rules.

NUpath is competency-based: approved attributes may be met through major or elective courses. This inventory does not fabricate all eligible class sections. BA-language, NYC-campus and nursing-specific general-education panels are not inherited by these Boston BS/BSEnvE degrees.

Permitted home-college options and their additional progression/graduation rules have not been exhaustively verified for this combined degree. Catalog hosting context is not assumed to fix the student’s designated home college.

All 14 degree-linked business concentrations are represented conditionally. At least one of 13 primary options is required; International Business is second-only. No concentration course pool is a list of universally required courses. Additional-concentration overlap and conditional elective limits remain controlling. Home-college applicability remains unresolved; curriculum is partial.

Admissions explicitly lists Khoury College of Computer Sciences and D’Amore-McKim School of Business as participating colleges. Family hosting units record that participation, not permitted or mandatory home-college designations. The scalar hosting unit remains unassigned; individual degree-awarding college and all applicable college-policy conditions require separate confirmation.

Prerequisites retain the published alternatives and grade thresholds; corequisites and recommended preparation are separately labelled in these notes. Missing prerequisite fields are unknown, not a claim of no prerequisite.

Concurrent-enrollment alternatives stay inside their published prerequisite conditions; separately labelled corequisites and timing advice remain notes. Explicit zero-hour recitations are verified zero, not unknown.

Data Science metadata consistency review (2026–2027): every currently listed DS course now has a guarded description and independent semester-hour value from the official subject catalog. Published prerequisite alternatives are preserved. DS 1300 has no explicit prerequisite in its reviewed block, so that field remains unknown. This review does not add any DS course to the degree requirements.

Writing, physics and philosophy metadata review (2026–2027): 4 existing course observations gain official subject-catalog descriptions, stated credits and explicit registration conditions. Physics concurrent-registration prose remains a separate note; advanced-writing prerequisite grade alternatives remain intact. College-related writing audiences do not assign a home college.
